section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Rate of Change
section_1.content: Briefly revisit the Average Rate of Change (secant line) to establish the foundation of measuring change over an interval.
section_1.example: A squirrel running between two trees: Distance / Time = Average Speed.

section_2.title: The Geometric Transition: Zooming In
section_2.content: Introduce the 'Magnifying Glass' metaphor. As the interval between two points approaches zero, the secant line transforms into a tangent line. This visualizes the derivative as the local slope.
section_2.example: Zooming into a curved roller coaster track until the segment appears as a perfectly straight line segment.

section_3.title: The Functional View: Sensitivity Analysis
section_3.content: Shift from geometry to transformation. Define the derivative as a 'sensitivity machine'—how an output value transforms in response to a tiny input perturbation.
section_3.example: A robotic arm's angle control: If I nudge the motor angle by 0.001 degrees, how much does the gripper position move?

section_4.title: The Dynamic Operator: Visualizing Change
section_4.content: Present the derivative not as a static number, but as an operator that maps one function to another, transforming 'position' functions into 'velocity' functions.
section_4.example: Animation showing a position graph (f) morphing into a velocity graph (f') in real-time as the derivative operator acts upon it.

section_5.title: Synthesis and Summary
section_5.content: Conclude that the derivative is a transformation of a state into its rate of change. Remind students that local linear approximation is the core of this transformational power.
